description: The city belongs to its people, not its machine. The Long Watch is an enduring underground movement that means to take the Coldwater Basin back from the Architect, and to have a city left standing when it does. They sabotage constantly and they are careful about what: a relay, a records floor, a vat hall, anything that serves the machine and nobody else. They will not touch the water, the grid or the trains, because they intend to inherit those, and a city nobody can live in is not worth taking. Where a thing is both at once they argue about it, and that argument is most of what a cell does with its evenings. They do not seek to transcend humanity; they seek to free it, and remain human while they do. Their finest wear no augment and carry no mutation, only a lifetime's honed discipline, and the unsettling habit of out-shooting the chromed and out-thinking the machine with nothing but a steady hand and everything they ever bothered to master. That last part is not an aspiration but an entry requirement: they will not train a body with metal in it or flesh that has gone its own way, and they will not be argued round. Come back cleansed, or do not come back.

flags.creed: The city belongs to its people, not its machine.

reader.experience: Run with the Long Watch and the underground opens to you: safehouses, honest quartermasters, people who'll hold a line at your back because you held one at theirs. You climb on nothing but what you master: a steadier hand, a sharper read, gear kept immaculate and skills drilled long past the point anyone thinks is reasonable. The fantasy here is the quiet one. Out-shooting the chromed over iron sights, out-thinking the machine with a paper map, and never once needing a single wire to do it. You stay human, and you make being human look like the unfair advantage. They keep no hall and no roster you could find; but those who've gone looking say the way in runs through the industrial east, past the machine's dead ends, to people who still fix things by hand, and that the Long Watch does not surface for you until you've truly decided whose side of the switch you're on. Understand what you are deciding. They do not take the chromed and they do not take the mutated, and the ones who go looking with wire under the skin are turned round at the door by people who are unfailingly polite about it. Whatever you are carrying has to come out first. Have the metal cut, have the flesh corrected, and present yourself in the body you started with; the Watch will note that you were once something else, and let you in anyway, and never quite stop mentioning it.
reader.path_text: The Human way. Stay as we are. No steel, no mutation, no psionics: the human form is not the problem, the machine's grip is. Held as a condition of membership, not a preference. Cleanse yourself before you ask them for anything.
reader.pull: Keep the lights on. Take back the switch.
reader.relnote: No agents have surfaced in the Basin. The Watch keeps to the dark.
tenets: The Basin belongs to its people, not its machine.
Preserve the infrastructure, reclaim its stewardship.
Reform civilization; stay human doing it.

name: The Long Watch
